stem: A nurse is preparing to transfer a client from bed to wheelchair. Which action best reflects safe patient-handling practice?

options.A: Use a gait belt and perform a one-person transfer before determining whether the client can bear weight or how much assistance is needed.
options.B: Manually lift the client's full body weight when the transfer distance is short and a second nurse is nearby.
options.C: Assess the client's mobility and assistance needs first, then use the recommended assistive equipment and number of staff for the transfer.
options.D: Begin the transfer without equipment and add a device only if the client becomes unstable while standing.

rationale: NIOSH identifies patient handling as a major source of musculoskeletal injury and recommends Safe Patient Handling and Mobility practices that use assistive lifting technology instead of unnecessary high-risk manual handling. VA's current SPHM program specifically uses patient-assessment algorithms to determine mobility/independence, select the safest handling method and equipment, and identify the number of staff needed for each task. Therefore C is correct. A begins a transfer before determining weight-bearing and assistance needs, B relies on manual lifting of full body weight, and D delays equipment selection until instability occurs rather than planning the transfer safely in advance.
educational_objective: Before transferring a client, assess mobility and assistance needs and use the appropriate assistive equipment and staffing level for the specific task rather than defaulting to manual lifting.
source_organization: CDC/NIOSH; U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs
source_document_title: About Safe Patient Handling and Mobility; Safe Patient Handling and Mobility (SPHM)
source_version_date: NIOSH page May 9, 2024; current VA SPHM guidance live-rechecked August 16, 2026
source_locator: NIOSH SPHM: patient handling is a major WMSD risk; use assistive lifting devices and safe patient-handling programs. VA SPHM: clinical/patient assessment algorithms select the right equipment and number of staff for each handling/mobility task; patient mobility tools assess mobility and degree of assistance and generate task-specific equipment/process recommendations.
source_claim_supported: Safe transfer planning should begin with assessment of patient mobility/assistance needs and then use appropriate assistive technology and staffing rather than routine manual lifting or waiting for instability.
blueprint_source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
blueprint_locator: Basic Care and Comfort: assist with mobility and transfers, use assistive devices appropriately, and promote safe movement/positioning while preserving client function and comfort.
blueprint_topic: Basic Care and Comfort — safe transfer assessment and assistive equipment

source_original.stem: A nurse is preparing to transfer a client from bed to wheelchair. Which action best reflects safe patient-handling practice?

options.A: Use a gait belt and perform a one-person transfer before determining whether the client can bear weight.
options.B: Manually lift the client’s full body weight when the transfer distance is short and a second nurse is nearby.
options.C: Assess the client’s mobility and assistance needs, then use appropriate assistive equipment and additional staff when indicated.
options.D: Begin the transfer without equipment, then add a device only if the client becomes unstable while standing.

source_original.rationale: NIOSH identifies patient handling as a major musculoskeletal-injury risk and recommends safe patient-handling and mobility strategies, including appropriate assistive lifting devices. Transfer planning should be based on the patient's mobility and assistance needs rather than routine manual lifting.
source_original.source_detail: Safe patient handling includes use of assistive lifting technology and appropriate procedures to reduce injury risk during lifting, moving, and repositioning. Source has no separate formal version identifier in the cited page metadata; live currentness and applicability rechecked 2026-08-15. NCSBN first-check: Client Needs — Physiological Integrity — Basic Care and Comfort: mobility, assistive devices, hygiene, nutrition, elimination, comfort and nonpharmacological basic-care activities as applicable. 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan; effective 2026-04-01 through 2029-03-31; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.

correction_summary: Retained the safe-transfer construct and key C, strengthened the keyed action using current VA patient-assessment algorithms that determine both equipment and staffing, tightened the distractors around premature/manual transfer, and set difficulty to medium because the final item requires selecting a safe assessment-first workflow rather than simple device recall.

audit_findings.clinical_category: Safe patient handling during bed-to-wheelchair transfer
audit_findings.source_authority: Current CDC/NIOSH SPHM guidance plus current VA SPHM assessment algorithms; NCSBN 2026 blueprint
audit_findings.currentness: NIOSH and VA SPHM pages live-rechecked 2026-08-16
audit_findings.exact_locator: NIOSH SPHM prevention strategies and VA SPHM patient-assessment/equipment/staffing algorithm descriptions
audit_findings.claim_audit: Final item uses the directly supported assessment-first/equipment/staffing workflow and does not prescribe a specific device without knowing the client's mobility or weight-bearing ability.

distractor_audit.A: Incorrect because a one-person gait-belt transfer should not be chosen before assessing mobility/weight-bearing/assistance needs.
distractor_audit.B: Incorrect because manual lifting of full body weight is a high-risk practice when assistive technology is indicated/available.
distractor_audit.D: Incorrect because safe equipment/staff selection occurs before the transfer, not only after instability develops.

audit_findings.ambiguity_second_answer: Only C follows the source-supported sequence of assessment followed by task-specific equipment and staffing selection.
audit_findings.cueing: All options describe transfer-planning approaches rather than unrelated fall-prevention actions.
audit_findings.blueprint: Basic Care and Comfort — mobility, transfers and assistive-device use.
audit_findings.independent_second_pass: Rechecked current NIOSH and VA SPHM guidance, assessment algorithms, all alternatives, rationale, objective, equipment/staffing wording, ambiguity, cueing and NCSBN Basic Care and Comfort alignment. C remained uniquely correct.
